newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Van Lanschot might float in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Van Lanschot might float in 1998.

text.p: Dutch F. van Lanschot Bankiers NV said on Wednesday it might float some of its shares in 1998 and that it would probably make a decision this autumn.
"There is not a final plan for a flotation, but we are considering such a move," said chairman Bert Heemskerk.
He said that Van Lanschot did not need extra funds in the current year, but that it might float some of its shares in 1998 to pay for its expansion plans.
Van Lanschot said it was planning to widen its business into life insurance and pension products in the Netherlands.
"We are on the lookout for a partner, but if we do not find one we could start this business ourselves," he said.
Van Lanschot might decide to start up its own insurance business in cooperation with Friesland Bank.
Friesland Bank, which holds a 21 percent stake in Van Lanschot, is in talks with the bank on joint investments in technology and high tech infrastructure.
"A further cooperation between Friesland Bank and Van Lanschot is quite possible in a few years time," said Heesmkerk.
Heemskerk said Van Lanschot had not spoken to its shareholders yet on the intended flotation.

Current shareholders are the Van Lanschot family with 12.5 percent, insurer Delta Lloyd with 8.5 percent, Nationale Investerings Bank 17 percent, Nederlandse Participatie Maatschappij, ABN AMRO, ING and unlisted insurer Achmea 6 percent each, investment fund Ducatus 11 percent and the remaining 6 percent are held by Van Lanschot personnel and pension fund.
Heemskerk said the possible flotation next year could also include an issue of new shares.
He said a float of at least 20 percent of the company was likely as less would not be substantial enough for a listing.
Earlier, Van Lanschot reported a 1996 net profit rise of over 30 percent to 73.1 million guilders.
The bank said it expected to increase profits by at least 10 percent in 1997.
